page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top centre. Page number at the top left. Catchword at the bottom right. No margin notes.

main_text.l: pitudines, fac ut in nos ipsos severe agamus, &
ab Animis nostris Reformatio incipiat, ut per-
spicaci Iudicio, & integro Corde accedentes, quae
in Ecclesia aut Statu perperam facta sunt, idonei si-
mus reformare.
Cor mundum crea in Nobis Deus & Spir-
itum rectum innova in visceribus nostris, ut tuo
ductu simul & tua Benedictione in Tuam omnia
Gloriam faciamus.
Miserere deformitatum & vulnerum, quae
temerarii & saevi Reformatores huic Ecclesiae &
Statui inflixerunt; exstingue Factionum flamma-
s sub praetextu Reformandi accensas.
Et quemadmodum per haec mutuo dissidia, &
confusiones palam omnibus facere voluisti quam
sint pravi nonnullorum fines; & infirma Iudicia;
ita ex his flammis educas nos purgationes, praeeun-
te Christiana magis, & plus in se charitatis ha-
bente Reformatione, ubi nihil vindictae aut am-
bitus, avaritiae denique aut sacrilegii polleat in
eorum consilia, quibus opus tam insigne & bo-
num, & jam maxime necessarium aequo & licito
more peragendum providentia tua demandave-
rit; ut internae pietatis felicitate auctiti ego simul
& populus etiam Pacis externa beneficio rectius
nobis[?] in posterum discamus.

page.notes: The bottom right shows "21.De", large type, which opens the next section; it is treated as a catchword. The word before "in posterum" at the end is partly obscured and reads as "nobis"; uncertain, marked [?]. The word "auctiti" is partly unclear and may be "auctifi"; the reading is uncertain. Long s in "fac" and "faciamus" is read as the word itself. The running head is Greek transliterated into Latin capitals, copied as printed.
